reason: Both answers are correct and cover the key points: exactly-once delivery is impossible, at-least-once plus an idempotent consumer is the standard, and a transactional outbox helps on the producer side. B states the delivery vs processing distinction more directly and explains why delivery fails (a lost message can't be told from a lost ack). It also addresses the teammate's likely source of the claim, naming Kafka EOS, SQS FIFO and Pub/Sub and what each does and doesn't cover. A is also correct, but its framing of the delivery/processing distinction is less direct.
